text:
Marta (AM): Quick escalation — VertexInc POC failing with 413 when uploading a large context bundle to embeddings. They attached a base64 blob thats ~13MB after encoding. Any quick unblock ideas?

Diego (SalesEng): Which endpoint? embeddings or content-ingest? Also can you paste the curl?

Marta (AM): POST /v1/embeddings. Their sample (redacted):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  --data '{"model":"embed-large","input":"<base64-payload>"}'
```

proxy-bot: gateway: 413, client=10.10.1.5, server=api.redwood.ai, request="POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1"

Clara (Support): Base64 overhead ~33% is expected. If raw was ~10MB it becomes ~13.3MB. Short-term: 1) ask them to gzip and send binary (application/octet-stream) or 2) presigned S3 PUT + pointer in JSON.

Ivy (Edge): Our edge nginx has max_body_size 10M by default. We can do a tenant-scoped bump for a short POC window but Ops approval required. Also corporate proxies sometimes drop earlier.

Noor (Security): Presigned S3 is fine with SSE-KMS. We can issue presigns with server-side encryption headers so their security team is comfortable. If they cannot use external storage, offer multipart upload with encrypted parts.

Diego (SalesEng): For rapid unblock propose: we provide an SSE-KMS presigned PUT, they upload gzipped binary via PUT, then POST embeddings with {"input_url":"s3://...","model":"embed-large"}. Saves base64 and bypasses edge limit.

Clara (Support): If they need single-call semantics: client can split into <8MB chunks, POST each and client-side aggregate vectors (mean pooling). We'll share example scripts.

Marta (AM): Customer asked about billing: will larger uploads change pricing?

Clara (Support): Short answer: not for embeddings unit price. Network/storage egress could increase. For POC we usually absorb minor bandwidth.

Noor (Security): I'll craft a one-pager about presign flow: SSE-KMS headers, minimal retention policy, limited IAM role for presign.

Ivy (Edge): If they insist on one big POST and are willing to accept risk, tag me and I'll open a temporary gateway exception (25M) scoped to their tenant CIDR and a 72h TTL. Need approval ticket.

Diego (SalesEng): I'll draft a quick node + curl example for presign + PUT + pointer call.

Marta (AM): Please send both the presign option and chunking script to Vertex infra. Ask them to run curl -v and paste the full response headers if they still see 413 so we can tell if it's their proxy.

Clara (Support): Copyable example for them:

```
# client: PUT gzipped binary to presigned URL
curl -X PUT "<presigned-url>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @bundle.zip.gz

# then call embeddings with pointer
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"embed-large","input_url":"s3://vertex-bucket/bundle.zip.gz"}'
```

Marta (AM): Thanks all — I'll send and follow up. Will loop back here with what Vertex says. :thumbsup:
